docs.title: Panel
docs.text: The Panel block allows placement of Widgets on the "panel" surface.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Panel can have the front and back of its surface tilted by using a Screwdriver to configure it. Additionally, you can place multiple panels side by side to connect them together.

docs.title: Signal Generator
docs.text: The Signal Generator is used to create Signals for usage with Antennas, as it allows you to control the Frequency of the signal. The dials in the Signal Generator allow both fine and coarse control over the generated Frequency.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Almost every block in Superposition interacts with Signals in one way or another. Every signal has Frequency, Amplitude, and usually Data.

docs.title: Frequency
docs.text: Many blocks in Superposition may create signals specifically to transfer data. These blocks with a standard frequency of 42 MHz. A Signal Generator may be used to create a signal with a specific frequency. This is usually important for signals that will be broadcasted with an antenna because

docs.title: Amplitude
docs.text: The Amplitude of a signal is important when broadcasting a signal as it has the biggest impact on the range of a signal. A signals amplitude is miniscule by default, and can be increased with an Amplifier. A signal that is not amplified will be too weak to be received by other antennas.

docs.title: Widgets
docs.text: Widgets are a collection of many small parts that can be placed on the surface of a Panel. They consist of Gauges, Buttons, Switches, Dials, and much more.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Much like blocks, Widgets can be configured with a Screwdriver by (shift) right-clicking their tooltip. This allows you to change many options, including the name and color of every widget.

docs.title: Screwdriver
docs.text: The Screwdriver can be used to configure blocks that have configurations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: When looking at a block, a configuration can be changed by right clicking, and scrolled by shift right clicking.
